newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco cuts price of phone calls.
newsitem.headline: Morocco cuts price of phone calls.

text.p: Morocco's Post Office on Tuesday announced cuts in the cost of international and mobile phone calls ranging from two to 31 percent. They take effect on New Year's day.
The biggest cuts bring the cost of calls to Argentina, Brazil and South Africa down to 22 dirhams ($2.50) per minute from 32 dirhams ($3.63).

The Post Office, in a statement, said: "These changes come within the framework ot the ONPT's tariff strategy, aimed to ensure large penetration of telecommunication products and services and development of their use."

The cost of calls to St Vincent, the Maldives, Virgin Islands and Diego Garcia are cut by six percent to 30 dirhams from 32 per minute. Conversation with Mauritania and Libya will cost two percent less at eight dirhams instead of 8.20 dirhams.

Countries are listed in 13 categories, with the price of calls to many European countries being reduced by 25 percent to nine dirhams from 12, and those to the United States falling to 14 dirhams per minute from 20 dirhams.
Calls to Middle East countries, including Bahrain and Egypt, Syria and Yemen will cost 23 percent less, at 14 dirhams a minute instead of 18.30 dirhams.
The lowest charge in future will be to neighbouring Algeria at six dirhams instead of 8.20 dirhams a minute.

Mobile telephone usage costs are also being cut, with subscription charges to the network falling to 800 dirhams from 1,400 dirhams, monthly charges dropping to 200 dirhams from 250, and the cost of calls being set at 3.20 dirhams from the current four dirhams.

The Moroccan parliament is at present debating a law on privatising the Office National des Postes et Telecommunications (ONPT), which envisages the postal and phone services being controlled by separate companies.
